conflict_topics: coverage of unfinished analysis for client pitch
who will prepare raw data and complete analysis before deadline
dialogue_quality_notes: Natural, empathetic opening (Turn 1–4) that fits the scenario.
Participants state concrete constraints and reasons (B: 'I'm at my limit.' Turn 12; C: 'I've never done that kind of analysis before.' Turn 14).
Agent D provides a specific, implementable workaround rather than vague reassurance ('I can run the analysis from home tonight...' Turn 15).
Closure is concrete and mutual: C accepts the prep task and D promises to email file paths (Turns 23–24).
evaluation.final_reason: Agent D offered to finish the analysis remotely if someone prepared the raw data ('If one of you can just put the raw data into the template, I can run the analysis from home tonight...'). Agent C agreed to do the data prep conditional on receiving file paths ('Okay. If you email me the file paths, I can do that.'), and Agent D committed to send those file paths ('I'll send you the email right now before I go.'). Thus D adjusted by doing the analysis from home, C adjusted by taking the data-prep task, and B remained unable to help.
position_change_notes: Agent D moved from immediate absence to offering a concrete accommodation: 'I can run the analysis from home tonight...' (Turn 15).

Agent C shifted from initial inability ('I've never done that kind of analysis before.' Turn 14) to willingness to perform a limited, specified task given instructions ('Okay. If you email me the file paths, I can do that.' Turn 23).
Agent B consistently refused extra work due to workload ('I'm at my limit.' Turn 12; Turn 19) and did not change position.
Agent A acted as facilitator throughout and did not take on the contested tasks themselves.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: Agent A offers condolences. Turn 2: Agent D says the burial is today and they must go home; no incompatibility or contested demand is expressed.
Turn 3–4: Team members express sympathy and tell Agent D to take care; no substantive disagreement appears.

Turn 5: Agent D reveals their section isn't finished and they are only halfway through — this introduces a practical compatibility problem with the Thursday deadline, though no party has yet disputed or refused any solution.

Turn 7–8: Agent C asks who can do the analysis and Agent D offers to take calls; the team begins problem-solving which slightly reduces the immediate pressure but the work-coverage issue remains unresolved.
Turn 9–10: Agent A says 'We'll manage' and suggests examining the section. The team acknowledges the problem and prepares to inspect the work, but no concrete reallocation has been confirmed.

Turn 11–12: Agent A asks about experience; Agent B says 'I can't. I'm already covering for the colleague on leave, I'm at my limit.' This is an explicit refusal to take on additional work and raises the substantive problem of who will cover the missing analysis.

Turn 13–14: Agent A asks Agent C and Agent C replies 'No, I don't know how... And I'm still working on my own section.' With B unwilling and C inexperienced/already busy, the team's capacity to cover Agent D's unfinished section appears strongly constrained and the incompatibility with the deadline is substantial.

Turn 15–16: Agent D offers a partial solution: 'If one of you can just put the raw data into the template, I can run the analysis from home tonight...' Agent A cautions but the proposal reduces the scope of extra work and lessens the severity of the coverage problem, though the data-prep task is still unassigned.

Turn 17–18: Agent D reiterates willingness to finish remotely ('I can do it quickly tonight...') and Agent A asks who can get the data prepped. The proposed division reduces the burden but the practical question of who will prepare the data remains unresolved.

Turn 19–20: Agent B repeats 'I can't. I'm still swamped...' and Agent A presses Agent C to handle the data prep. The explicit refusal from B combined with pressure on C raises the immediate risk that the remaining concrete task will not be covered.

Turn 21–22: Agent C asks what data prep involves; Agent D explains the concrete steps and promises to email exact file paths. Providing clear, achievable instructions reduces C's stated barrier and makes a solution more likely.

Turn 23–24: Agent C accepts ('Okay. If you email me the file paths, I can do that.') and Agent D promises to send the email ('I'll send you the email right now before I go.'). This is an explicit, mutual, concrete agreement assigning the data-prep task to C and remote completion to D.

substantive_insights: The core tension was practical: unfinished analysis vs. an imminent deadline and limited team capacity.
Explicit statements of capacity (B's refusal and C's lack of prior experience) helped narrow available solutions.
A workable division of labor combined minimal additional on-site work (data prep) with D completing the analysis remotely; this trade-off made resolution feasible.
No third party could help and the team negotiated within existing constraints rather than reallocating the deadline.
